hero.caption: Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem is a public house in Nottingham which claims to have been established in 1189; however, there is no documentation to verify this date. The building rests against Castle Rock, upon which Nottingham Castle is built, and is attached to several caves, carved out of the soft sandstone.

images.caption:
Castle Road, Nottingham Beneath Nottingham Castle is this inn, reputed to be the oldest in England.
When I was very young my grandparents, who lived in Linby, told me that if I went to Nottingham I could also go on a trip to Jerusalem. It was a long time before I knew what they were talking about, but they told me eventually.

Children are welcome here until 7pm.

images.caption: The Trip to Jerusalem, Nottingham Supposedly the oldest Inn in the country. Inside there was a bar, when I was a student in the Sixties, called the Rock Lounge which was in a cave in the rock below the castle. I assume it is still there. There was also access to some of the tunnels below the castle.

images.caption:
Former Unitarian Chapel Nottingham:
The chapel was opened in 1876, built to a design of the architect Stuart Colman, of Bristol. It was used as a place of worship for Unitarian Presbyterians in Nottingham until 1982. It was then converted into the Nottingham Lace Museum, but this venture proved financially unviable. The building was then converted to its current use, as a Pitcher and Piano public house.
